title: The Potter's Donkey and the Royal War Elephant (PT)
summary: An imperial war elephant mocks an ordinary potter's donkey on a muddy road. When a flash flood strikes, the donkey's agile hoofs save the day.
full_text:
During an imperial march through the lowlands of Bengal during the monsoon, a colossal war elephant named Gajraj—armor-plated, tusks tipped with steel, and carrying a golden howdah—trotted along the muddy highway. An ordinary village potter was leading his small, grey donkey laden with clay cooking pots on the road shoulder.

The elephant's proud mahout shouted: 'Clear the road, you wretched potter! Get that miserable, scrawny donkey out of the path of the Emperor's mighty war elephant!'

The elephant trumpeted loudly, spraying muddy water over the humble donkey.

A sudden flash flood rushed down from the swollen river, washing away the wooden bridge ahead and turning the clay road into a treacherous, bottomless quagmire of deep, sucking mud!

The colossal, five-ton war elephant stepped into the mud. Under its immense weight, its massive feet sank deep into the mire! The heavy beast struggled, panicked, and sank down to its belly, completely trapped and sinking deeper with every movement!

Soldiers pushed and pulled, but five tons of thrashing elephant could not be moved from the deep mud.

Meanwhile, the potter's little donkey, weighing barely two hundred pounds, possessed light, small, agile hooves. Stepping lightly from stone to grass hummock, the donkey trotted effortlessly across the mud without sinking an inch!

Seeing the soldiers in distress, the potter unhooked his donkey's pack ropes, tied them to a long dry rope, and had the agile donkey carry the lifeline across the mud to a sturdy banyan tree on the opposite dry bank!

With the rope secured to the tree, thirty soldiers pulled with a winch, helping the trapped elephant haul itself safely out of the sucking mire onto solid ground!

Emperor Akbar, who had watched the drama from horseback, embraced the potter and stroked the donkey's wet ears:

'Look at that, Birbal! The mighty war elephant that can smash fortress gates sank helpless in common mud, while the humble potter's donkey trotted across the mire and saved the giant beast!'

Birbal smiled with deep philosophical warmth:

'Sire, in the great tapestry of life, the elephant has its strength for battle, and the donkey has its lightness for the mud.

'Never despise the humble, for when the ground beneath your feet becomes treacherous, the smallest creature may be the only one who can carry you to safety.'

Akbar rewarded the potter with a purse of gold and ordered all mahouts to treat working animals with respect.
moral: Lição de moral: Wit beats power
